newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa product exports steady in February.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa product exports steady in February.

text.p: Ivory Coast's semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports were steady in February at 8,830 tonnes, after 8,864 tonnes for January, but up from 6,451 tonnes in February 1996, official shipping data show.
The year-on-year rise stems from new processing factory capacity coming on line as Ivory Coast seeks to add value to exports.

Cumulative exports in the first five months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season -- including shipments from October 1 to October 24 when the season opened -- were 40,703 tonnes, against 23,745 in 1995/96.
The data do not separate liquor, butter and cake exports but powder shipments totalled 450 tonnes.
Cumulative powder shipments stand at 2,627 tonnes this season against 1,863 tonnes the year before and 38 tonnes in 1994/95.
French ports were the main destination in February 1997, accounting for 2,296 of product exports. European ports accounted for 3,491 tonnes of the total.
